notes_list.title: Kolbe–Schmitt Carboxylation
notes_list.basic_overview: Sodium phenoxide reacts with carbon dioxide under pressure and heat to form salicylate, which gives salicylic acid after acidification.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
The transformation introduces CO2-derived carbon at the ortho position relative to oxygen. Industrially relevant conditions use elevated pressure and temperature. Exam clue: phenoxide + CO2 → salicylic acid after acidification.

MECHANISM & STEPWISE EXPLANATION
Phenoxide reacts with carbon dioxide under pressure/heat to give an ortho-carboxylated product after acidification.
